A line about who you are
Goblins harry the roads out of the Ember Crown. The guild posts a standing bounty: thin their numbers in the wilds.
Bryn's forge runs cold without ore. Bring iron from the northern hills so the smith can arm the town.

keys: # --- Phase 34.5C: the Frostfang clan arc and its betrayal branch ---

en: Hjalvar Stormbound will not take an outsider's word for anything. The rime that drifts down from the passes is a problem the hold has stopped bothering to name. Break four of them.
Sigrun counts the stores twice and does not like the second number. Pelts, off whatever will spare them, before the long dark closes the passes.
What Comes Up Through the Ice
Something walks the ice that stopped being anyone a long time ago. The clans have a word for the Hollow and it is not a polite one. Put five of them down.
Halvar One-Hand watches the hold's fires from outside them and has an offer for anyone the hold has not yet claimed. Three of their raiders, and he will believe you mean it.
The shamans are what hold the clans together in the cold. Halvar wants two of them silenced, and has a buyer in the south who wants the same.
The notice board bristles with contracts. One fresh bounty catches your eye.
BOUNTY: Goblins prey on our roads. Cull three in the wilds and the guild pays in coin. Take the contract?
The contract is yours. Goblins haunt the wilds beyond the walls — go earn your coin.
The bounty still stands: three goblins, not yet culled.
The bounty is settled — the guild thanks you. Watch the board for more.
Bryn looks up from a cold anvil, soot dark on his brow.
The forge — is it burning again?
My forge is dead without ore. Bring me three lumps of iron from the hills and I'll keep the town in steel. Will you?
Bless you. The hills lie to the north — mind the goblins along the way.
Still cold, this forge. Three lumps of iron ore — that's all I ask.
The iron you brought has the forge roaring again. Steel for the town at last — my thanks.
Mirela grinds herbs with a worried frown, her shelves near bare.
Goblin wounds fill my cot and my remedies run dry. Four sprigs of healing herb from the wilds would save lives. Will you gather them?
Thank you. The herb grows in the wilds — look for the pale green leaves.
My shelves are still bare. Four sprigs of healing herb, when you can.
With these herbs the wounded will mend. You've done more than you know — thank you.
These raids are no accident. A warband masses in the northern wilds, and its captain means to burn us out. Cut down five of them and you break its nerve. Will you stand for the Ember Crown?
Then the Flame go with you. Strike at the heart of them in the northern wilds.
The warband still gathers. Five of them, traveller — break their nerve.
You broke the warband. The Ember Crown will sing your name by the hearth tonight — take the smith's finest steel, you have more than earned it.
The Iron King bars your path.
The Iron King's fire guts the air where he fell, a fragment of fallen divinity beating like a second heart. It is yours to take. Will you absorb the flame?
Power floods you, hot and total, and somewhere far back something dims to make room for it. The bargain is struck.
You turn from it. The fire gutters, unclaimed, and the cold rushes back in to fill the dark.
Level up!  You are now level {0}
Kael Aldemar will not take a stranger at his back. Cut down the goblins raiding the wilds and he will judge for himself what you are.
Cut down goblins in the wilds
Kael's sword-brother Toren fell in the northern wilds, and the goblins picked the Emberguard dead. Recover what they carried off.
The knight looks up from a whetstone and a blade that needs no sharpening.
Kael Aldemar. Last shield of the Emberguard, for whatever that's worth now. The order burned with the rest — I'm what the fire left standing.
You look like you're waiting for something.
I'm waiting to see what you do. Goblins are bleeding the roads while the guild counts coin. Cut four of them down out in the wilds. Then we'll talk about walking together.
I fight for my own reasons.
Good. Don't come back and tell me about it. Come back having done it.
Then the roads still bleed. Go.
I heard. The road's quieter than it was yesterday — that's not nothing. Say the word and my shield goes where you go.
Sworn, then. Not to a crown — to you. Try not to make me regret the difference.
Toren. My sword-brother. He held the pass at Ashfall so the rest of us could run, and the goblins picked his bones after. What they carried off is out there in their camps. I'd have it back.
Their camps are north. Take what they took.
I found what the ash left.
That's his. That's — yes. Twelve years I carried that pass, and I couldn't put it down. You reached back for a dead man you never met. I'll not forget it.
It's enough. He's carried now. Ask me for anything.
Do you ever think about stopping?
Every day. Then I look at where we're going and I think: someone has to walk in first. Might as well be the one who's already burned.
As you say. I'll be here, sharpening a blade that doesn't need it. Come back when you need a shield.
For a thousand years the world has been dying.
The gods are dead. Magic fades. Dragons have gone from the skies.
Seven champions were made to set it right. The Flamebearers.
Six fell — to corruption, to power, to the enemy itself.
You are the seventh, {0}. The last hope of Embervale, or its last ruin.
Move the mouse to look around
Press {0} and the surrounding keys to walk
Look at someone and press {0} to speak or use
Press {0} to open your character screen
Press {0} to read your quest journal
Press {0} to cast your prepared spell
The brazier is cold. The warband still holds the north.
The Iron King is ash, and his ember burns behind your ribs. It is warm. That is what frightens you.
The Iron King is ash. You let his ember go out — and felt, for a moment, how easy it would have been not to.
Far to the north, past the frozen sea, something older than a fallen king turns its attention south.
EMBERVALE — Vertical Slice.  Your story continues in Frostfang Reach.
The guild says you know every sword in this town.
Every one worth naming. Why — are you looking to share the road?

Then look for Kael Aldemar, in the square. Emberguard, before the Emberguard stopped being anything. He came back from Ashfall alone and he has been sharpening that blade ever since. Ask him yourself — he will not offer.
So I see. Good. He has carried that pass alone long enough — let him carry something forward instead.
You keep looking north like it owes you something.

I look north because I remember. A fallen champion's fire does not simply go out when you cut them down — it looks for a new hand to hold it. I have seen a man take that warmth for himself, meaning to do good with it. We buried what was left of who he had been. If you ever stand over one of them with the choice in front of you, remember that he meant well too.

keys: # --- Phase 33D: elder conversation moved off literals (CLAUDE.md §6) ---

en: (Greet the elder like an old friend.)
I'm still searching for that iron.
(Clasp his hand — your heart is still your own.)
(He flinches at your gaze. Ask what troubles him.)
The Flame keeps us both, elder.
(Say nothing. Let the ember within stir.)
Well met, traveller. Our smith's forge runs cold — we've no iron to feed it.
Three lumps of iron ore from the northern hills would set us right. Will you help?
Bless you. The hills lie to the north — mind the goblins along the way.
The forge still waits. Three lumps of ore — you'll find them in the hills to the north.
You brought the iron — the forge burns bright again. The village won't forget it.
Good to see you again, friend. The forge runs hot, thanks to you.
The elder meets your eyes and nods slowly. 'A steady soul — rarer than iron, these days. The Flame keeps you, traveller.'
'There is an ember in your gaze I do not trust — ash where the light should be. I have seen it before, and it does not end gently. Tread carefully, traveller.'
A broad man in wolf-hide watches you cross his hold without rising. 'Southerner. You walked in through the cold, so you are either useful or lost.'

'The Stormbound hold it, and eight clans besides — hunters, tamers, shamans. We do not answer to your guilds and we do not sit in your councils. Out here a name is what you carry, not what you are given.'
'Fear is a soft word. The Storm Tyrant took the high passes and calls it grief. He was a Flamebearer once, same as your Iron King. They all end the same way — certain.'
She looks you over the way she'd look over a sled dog — teeth first. 'Stores are counted. Twice.'
Do the clans trade with outsiders?
'With outsiders who have stood a winter here, yes. You have stood an afternoon. Come back when the hold knows your name and we will talk about what is mine to give.'
Something large shifts in the dark behind her and settles again at a word you don't catch. 'Stand still. They judge quickly.'
'No. Frost-stalkers, whelped and raised. A hound obeys. These agree, for a while, and the day they stop agreeing is a day you want to be elsewhere.'
'Not the way you mean. The Sylthari sing at them and call it conversation. I feed them, I bleed for them, and I do not lie to them. That is the whole of it.'
The old man feeds the fire without looking up. 'Sit or don't. The cold has no opinion either way.'
'Older than the Ember Crown's walls, and it was never besieged, because there was never anything here worth the march. Ask me again when your south has burned down twice.'
'There is always work. Whether it is yours is a different question.'
He does not stand, but he moves along the bench, which from him is a ceremony. 'Sit. You carried what you said you would. The hold has your name now and it will not give it back.'

'Rime drifts down from the high passes and cuts whoever walks into it. We step around it. That is what stepping around a thing for twenty years looks like — a hold that has stopped calling it a problem. Break four. Then we will talk about what you are.'
'They do not bleed and they do not tire. Hit them until they stop being a shape.'
'Four. The passes are north of here and the cold does the counting.'
'Cleared. Twenty years and a stranger does it in an afternoon.' He does not sound pleased, exactly. 'The hold will use your name now. Do not make us regret teaching it.'

'Husks. They come up through the ice where the ice is thin, and they were people once, which is the part the young ones cannot get past. Five of them. Do not look at their faces and you will be fine.'
'Good. Yrsa will not send the stalkers after them — they will not go. That should tell you something.'
'Still walking, are they. Then you are not finished.'
'Done, and done without asking what it was worth first.' He is quiet a moment. 'You eat at the hearth from tonight. That is not a small thing and I will not say it twice.'
'I did. And here you are, with the hold using your name like it always did.' She sets down the tally. 'So. Stores.'

'Pelts. Five, off whatever out there can spare them, and I do not mean the stalkers — those are Yrsa's and she counts them too. The passes close in a month and a hold that is short in a month is a hold that is short all winter.'
'Wolves off the ice will do. Bring them whole — I can tell when a thing was skinned in a hurry.'
'Five. I said five and the number has not moved since.'
She weighs them the way she weighed you, and this time nods. 'Sworn to the stores, then. You are on the tally now — which means when it is short, it is partly your fault. Welcome to it.'
'I heard. They have not settled on you yet — but they stopped watching the door when you came through it, and that is most of the way there.'
Sigrun has me on the tally.
The old man finally looks up. 'Sworn to the stores. That is the one that counts, whatever the chief says over his bench. A hold is what it has in the cellar when the passes shut.'
and the branch that sells them out
A man sits at a fire too far from the hold's to be an accident, warming one hand and a stump. 'Southerner. You are the first thing to walk this way in a season that was not weather.'

'Hjalvar happened to it. There was a judgement, and there were eight clans in the room, and none of them was mine by the end of it.' He turns the stump to the fire. 'I do not dispute the judgement. I dispute surviving it out here.'
'I want the hold to be smaller. There are men in the south who want the same thing and pay for it, which makes us partners rather than friends.'

'It is. The rites are broken and the hold knows exactly whose hand did it — both of ours, and only one of us is easy to find.' He almost smiles. 'The Syndicate has your name now. That is worth more than mine and costs about the same.'

'Three of their raiders. Not for the killing — for the proof. Everyone who comes to this fire says they owe the hold nothing, and every one of them walks back down to it by dark. Three, and I will believe you.'
No. They've done nothing to me.
'Understand what you have agreed to. They will not forget it and there is no judgement out here to appeal to. There is only what you can carry.'
'Three. The patrols run the low ground by day and they do not look up.'

'Three, and you came back to say so.' He counts coin into the snow rather than your hand. 'The Syndicate keeps names. Yours is on a list now, and lists are the closest thing to a clan you will get south of here.'
'Two shamans. Raiders are replaceable — every hold breeds more. The rites are not. Kill the storm out of them and the eight clans are eight cold camps arguing about firewood by spring.'
'They call the weather down on you before they close. Do not let them finish. That is the whole of the advice I have.'
'Two. And you will hear the second one coming — they never learn not to sing.'
He listens to the wind for a while, which is only wind now. 'Twenty years I sat here waiting for that quiet. It is not what I thought it would sound like.' The coin comes anyway.

keys: # Names for the three bespoke-factory creatures (Phase 34G — were hard-coded English)
# Bestiary (BestiaryPanel) — the Ash Hunters' field journal

en: Seen, not yet understood. {0} more to fill the page.
Scavengers of the valley's edge, bold in numbers and cowardly alone. They have no forges of their own; every blade they carry was somebody else's first.
Ashfall's roads emptied of soldiers long before they emptied of travellers. These are the people who noticed. Fast, poorly armoured, and never encountered singly.
They call the burning a mercy. Zealots of the Fallen do not retreat, do not bargain, and do not appear to feel the fire they carry.
Armour still bearing a dead lord's colours, worn by something that no longer answers to him. They hold a shield line out of habit — the habit outlasted the man.
The Iron Syndicate does not send warnings. An enforcer waits without moving for as long as the contract requires, and the first sign of one is usually the last.
They do not charge. They fan wide, take the flanks, and wait for the pack-mate you turned your back on. Killing the first one teaches you nothing about the other three.
Twice the mass of the pack it leads and slower for it, which matters less than you would hope. Ash Hunters price a dire wolf pelt at four ordinary ones and still consider it cheap.
Frostfang's cats do not stalk so much as wait, buried to the eyes, for a week if need be. Struck first it dies easily. It is rarely struck first.
Blind past ten paces and entirely uninterested in you until you are inside that ten. Then it does not stop, does not tire, and does not recognise a wound as an argument.
Grazes the grey meadows where nothing else will. It runs long before it is threatened and cannot be caught on foot — the hide is worth the arrow it costs.
What the Hollow Queen leaves when she is finished. It notices you late, and then it simply does not stop coming. There is no fear left in it to work with.
It still keeps the guard rhythm it was drilled in — up, down, up — long after the flesh that learned it went. Wait out the cycle. It cannot break the habit and it will not retreat.
Lies in the ground where it was laid and does not stir for the passing. It stirs for the digging. Whatever it was buried with, it still counts as its own.
Kill the husks and she knits them back together; kill her and they stay down. Every Ash Hunter learns this in the same order, and most learn it the wrong way round first.
Cold, quick and barely there — three of them will surround you before one of them touches you. Steel finds them, which is the only mercy in it.

Set to guard something by a civilisation that has been dust for an age. It has not been relieved, so it is still on duty. The wind-up before it swings is long enough to read, and that is the whole fight.
Bound to a doorway rather than a master. Arcane force slides off it — a fact worth knowing before you commit to a spell — and it will come apart before it will step aside.
Small, fast, and never alone. Best understood as the ruin's immune response: individually trivial, collectively how expeditions end.
A knot of live fire that answers to nothing. Fighting one with flame is a lesson most only need once — it drinks what it is made of.
It does not chase. It freezes the ground you were going to stand on and waits for you to arrive there anyway.
Its lightning does not stop at the first target. Fight one at a distance from your companions, or fight it twice.
Not a creature so much as a spell that outlived its caster and kept the intent. It wards itself unprompted, and it strips whatever ward you were relying on.
A beast the corruption took whole. Whatever it used to be knew when to run; this does not. The Ash Hunters count it as game, but only just.
A Fallen who kept enough of themselves to cast and lost everything else. The lifedrain it works on you is the same rite the Marked are offered — it simply accepted first.
The lesser Fallen: robed, smouldering, and convinced. It throws fire because fire is all it has left to say.

The First Flamebearer. He was given the ember to save the world and concluded that a world worth saving would have to be held still to do it. He is not wrong about the danger. He is wrong about everything after.

Shield, axe, and a patience the south mistakes for slowness. A raider will let you walk past a dozen times; the clans count a stranger's crossings before they count his coin. Start something and you learn what the shield was for.
She hunts the way her stalkers do — wide, quiet, and never quite where you looked. The beasts are not commanded so much as agreed with, which is worse: cross her and there is no order to countermand.
The clans do not pray to Nyth. They listen to the weather and answer it, and what answers back is cold enough to stop a heart mid-beat. She mends her own before she ever turns the storm on you.

keys: # Phase 35A — dragons. The Ash and Ancient variants get their own entries in 35E/35F.

en: Older than the guilds, older than the Sundering, and entirely uninterested in either. A wild dragon claims a stretch of mountain and defends it against everything that walks — no cause, no bargain, no god. The Ash Hunters' advice is one line long: it turns slowly.

keys: # Phase 35E — the Ash dragon. Its own creature
en: not a corrupted Wild one (see LORE "Ash Dragons").

What Morthul makes of a dragon. It does not hoard, it does not claim a mountain, it does not care that you are there — it simply keeps going until the ground behind it is grey. The Hunters have no advice for this one. There is no safe side.

keys: # Phase 35F — the Ancient dragon. The one creature in the bestiary the player can talk to.

en: There were never many, and there are fewer now. An Ancient does not hoard gold or hold a mountain; it holds words, which is the only thing left worth keeping from before the gods died. It will talk to you. That is not the same as it being safe, and the Ash Hunters would like it noted that the last party to test the difference is still up there.
The Ancient in the northern aerie will not go east itself. It says the thing in the ash roost was a dragon once, and that this is the sort of errand younger, shorter-lived things are for.
Kill the Ash dragon in the eastern roost
The head comes down slowly, until one eye is level with you and considerably larger. 'You climbed all of that to look at me. Speak, then, small thing, and be interesting about it.'

'Old. That is the whole of it, and it took a very long time. I was here when the sky had gods in it and I was here the morning it did not. Your kind writes that down as an age. I remember it as weather.'
They say your kind keeps what the world forgot.

'Keeps. Yes. Not guards — nothing has come for it in eight hundred years. The Weave thins and your casters shout louder to be heard through it, and none of them think to ask the thing that learned to speak before the thinning started. So: keeps. Like a cellar keeps wine no one drinks.'

'I am looking at what is in you. I have seen that grey before, on my own kin, in the east. It does not stop, you understand. It is not a wound. It is an opinion the world is having about you, and it wins arguments slowly.'

'East of here, past the hold, something is sleeping in a roost that used to belong to a dragon. It still has the shape. Morthul is thorough about shapes. I will not go — I have watched enough of my kin become that, and I will not be the one who ends this one. You are younger. You have fewer things to remember afterward. Kill it.'
'Then go while you still think it is a favour to me. Take the cold seriously and the ash more so. It breathes rot, not fire — whatever you wore against my western cousin will not help you.'
The thing in the east still lives.
'I know. I would feel it stop. Go back down, or stay and talk — I have had centuries of practice at waiting and you have not.'

The great head turns aside for a long moment. 'I felt it. Thank you is a small word and I have not needed it in some time, so you will have the other kind of payment. There is one word I have never given away. It is not a spell your teachers could sell you; there is no one alive to sell it.'

It speaks, once, quietly, and the air between you disagrees about being air. When your ears work again the word is simply there, sitting behind your teeth, patient. 'Now there are two of us who know it. Do not be careless with the only copy.'

keys: # Phase 35G — the frost drake: the dragon you can meet by accident.

en: A dragon that never finished becoming one. Drakes do not fly, do not hoard and do not talk; they hold a stretch of snow and breathe cold at anything crossing it. The Ash Hunters rate them the most dangerous thing in the Reach that is not worth a song, and lose people to them every winter for exactly that reason.
It is already dead. I found the east roost before I found you.
